- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price movements; apply a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast starting from day of sentiment shift.
- Model tends to overfit short-term volatility; smooth 30-day forecast by averaging last 10–15 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
